display.title: Every Day Counts: Sefirah, Time, and Miriam's Lost Dime
display.summary_short: Why we count the days of Sefirah: time is a precious gift from Hashem. A funny story about a girl who keeps crying over a lost dime shows why we should not waste what we have now.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show during Sefiras HaOmer, on the midah of guarding time (shmiras hazman). Uncle Yossi points out that during Sefirah all we do is count days, and even make a brachah on it, because every day matters and each day should be one step higher than the day before. Time cannot be bought, stopped or slowed, and time that is lost never comes back. He tells of little Miriam, who lost a dime and kept crying even after her mother gave her more, because she was still thinking of the one she lost; her mother laughs that no amount will help until she stops mourning the lost dime and takes care of the ones she has. Like a person who loves to count his jewels, we count our days and fill them with Torah and mitzvos, and Hashem rewards us with long life, as the second paragraph of the Shema says.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: do not waste it or cry over what is lost, but fill each new day with Torah and mitzvos and make it better than the one before.
